The brand works with selected craftspeople and prefers those in the country where a material comes from. Some furniture is available in bespoke finishes and sizes. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:bitossi-ceramiche.name: Bitossi Ceramiche
paragraphs: Bitossi Ceramiche is a ceramics maker in Montelupo Fiorentino, Tuscany, Italy, founded in 1921 by Guido Bitossi as Manifattura Maioliche Artistiche Guido Bitossi. It produces ceramic objects such as vases, each piece made by hand in its factory. Aldo Londi directed its creative work in the 1950s, and Ettore Sottsass began working with the company in 1955.

The company continues to collaborate with designers including Max Lamb, Patricia Urquiola and Rooms Studio, and offers exclusive and tailor-made collections. It is now run by Ginevra Bocini Bitossi, the fourth generation of the family. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:tolix.name: Tolix
paragraphs: Tolix is a French furniture maker founded in 1927 in Autun, Burgundy. It produces steel chairs, stools, benches, tables, storage and accessories for indoor and outdoor use, and introduced galvanisation to French furniture manufacturing. The T37 chair was created for the 1937 Paris world exhibition and was reissued in 2023.

Each piece is built in series through manual steps: cutting, stamping, bending, welding, sanding and painting, with quality checked at every stage. Collections are made in Autun or by selected European partners, and the company keeps a showroom in Paris, open by appointment. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:new-works-dk.name: New Works DK
paragraphs: New Works is a Danish design company based in Copenhagen, founded in 2015 by Nikolaj Meier and Knut Bendik Humlevik. It offers furniture, lighting and objects, including the New Works Shelving System with an online configurator, and modular sofas such as Shore and Coda.

The company works with an international group of designers and craftspeople interested in sculptural forms and natural materials, and lists tactile qualities and craftsmanship among its values. A small team runs the brand from its office in Bredgade. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:no-early-birds.name: No Early Birds
paragraphs: No Early Birds is a Swedish furniture brand with its showroom in Stockholm, led by designer and architect Per Söderberg. It makes coffee and console tables, desks, chairs, stools, benches, storage and shelving, along with lamps, candelabras and mirrors. The main collection is built around an architectural cross-leg and a concealed mounting system.

The furniture is made in Sweden, and a separate Bespoke Collection is offered alongside the main range. The showroom on Östermalmsgatan is open Tuesday to Saturday or by appointment. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:grain.name: Grain
paragraphs: Grain is an American design studio and workshop on Bainbridge Island, Washington, founded in 2008 by Chelsea and James Minola, who met as industrial design students at the Rhode Island School of Design. It makes furniture, lighting and rugs, including Dish Side Tables in reclaimed Douglas fir and Stitch Mirrors sewn with hemp twine.

Work is made to order in its own shop or with artisans in North America, in small batches, and most designs can be sized and finished to custom requests. The studio combines current manufacturing technology with traditional craft techniques. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:unico-milano.name: Unico Milano
paragraphs: Unico Milano is an online furnishing brand, Milanese in name and outlook but sourcing its products from suppliers around the world rather than making them in Milan or Italy. The range covers sideboards, seats, tables, coffee tables, lights and tableware, chosen for a minimalist, functional look.

The brand sells through its own online shop, with a separate page for trade customers and a "shop the look" section that groups pieces together. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Sideboards, seats, tables, lights and tableware

makers:par-en-par.name: Par en Par
paragraphs: Par en Par is an Argentine design brand that makes furniture and home objects combining art and design, from stools and tables to consoles, armchairs, beds, lamps and rugs. Materials named on the site include recycled plastic, lacquered and reclaimed wood, and folded sheet steel with epoxy paint.

The work is built on collaboration with a network of craftspeople, designers and creatives, and pieces are produced as limited editions in small quantities. Many items are made to order, with delivery times of 60 to 90 days. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:stackelbergs.name: Stackelbergs
paragraphs: Stackelbergs is a family-owned Swedish maker of mohair and wool throws, blankets and accessories, founded by Anna-Carin Stackelberg and active for more than 15 years. Its range includes a collection with Carl and Karin Larsson, inspired by their home.

The throws are designed in Sweden and produced by partner producers in Italy, South Africa and Ukraine using traditional craft methods, with handmade fringes. Customised products are offered for projects with special design requirements, and the range is sold through shops across Europe. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Wool and mohair throws and blankets

makers:joris-poggioli.name: Joris Poggioli
paragraphs: Joris Poggioli is an architect and designer of French-Italian heritage who has worked on furniture, lighting and objects under his own name since 2017. The pieces are sculptural, with the emphasis on form and on materials such as black bronze, marble, onyx and rosewood. The 2025 series of numbered models includes a bench, chair, stool and desk.

Many pieces are listed as limited editions of 12, and some are numbered and signed. Lead times are given as 12 to 14 weeks. Alongside the design work, the practice also takes on architecture projects. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:parachilna.name: Parachilna
paragraphs: Parachilna is a lighting brand founded in 2013 and based in Colonia Güell, Santa Coloma de Cervelló, near Barcelona, Spain. It builds on the Riera family's lighting history, which began in the 1930s with Metalarte. The range covers pendant, floor, wall and ceiling, table and outdoor lights in collections such as Aballs, Babel, Gweilo, Petra and Topuro.

Parachilna works with a circle of designers including Jaime Hayon, Sebastian Herkner, Stephen Burks, Neri&Hu and Atelier Oï. Components come from European suppliers and production relies on highly manual methods, with lights designed to be demountable and repairable. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:master-master.name: Master & Master
paragraphs: Master & Master is a Czech furniture and accessories brand founded by Luděk Šteigl and Ondřej Zita, with a workshop in Zábřeh na Moravě and a showroom in Prague. The range covers seating such as the Mistra stackable chair, tables, shelving, and the Materra ceramic lamp designed with Tomáš Král.

Most of the collection is made in the Zábřeh workshop, with prototyping through to final assembly kept in-house. Metal and solid wood are the main materials, with plywood also used. The company can respond to individual requests from clients and architects. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:verpan.name: Verpan
paragraphs: Verpan is a design company that reissues and reinterprets the work of the Danish architect and designer Verner Panton, in cooperation with Verner Panton Design AG. Its catalogue covers lighting, furniture and accessories, including the Moon Opal pendant, the Cloverleaf Sofa and the System 1-2-3 Dining Chair.

Verpan works with suppliers and logistics partners on production and packaging, and designs its products for easy assembly and disassembly so that damaged parts can be replaced. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:made-by-hand.name: Made by Hand
paragraphs: Made by Hand is a Danish design brand founded in 2014, with a showroom and office in Copenhagen. It offers lighting, furniture and objects such as rugs and throws, developed with designers including Thor Høy, Boris Berlin and David Thulstrup. The Knit-Wit and Flying lamps are knitted by Kobleder, a family company in Austria.

Designers are paired with makers in several countries. Metalworkers in the Danish countryside produce the Workshop lamp, the NABLA rugs are made by the Milan firm Golran together with workshops in India, and the PePo lamp is mouth-blown glass. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:g-a-d.name: G.A.D
paragraphs: G.A.D is a Swedish furniture maker founded in 1997 by Kristian Eriksson, with its workshop in Hemse on Gotland. It makes tables, seating and storage in solid wood, in series including Ala, Högklint, Klinte, Roma and Stack. Each piece is numbered and signed by the craftsperson who built it.

Every piece is built to order and treated as an individual project. Klinte, Roma and Högklint can also be configured through an online furniture builder. Showrooms are in Stockholm, Gothenburg and Visby. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:coco-flip.name: Coco Flip
paragraphs: Coco Flip is a furniture and lighting design studio in Melbourne, Australia, founded in 2010 by Kate Stokes and Haslett Grounds. The studio designs lights and furniture, among them the Dancer lights, which are handcrafted in Melbourne from mid-fire clay together with ceramicist Belinda Wiltshire.

Production is small batch and local, with most pieces made to order and a select few kept in stock. The studio works with local makers and skilled artisans, and its showroom in Northcote is open by appointment. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:mor.name: MOR
paragraphs: MOR is a design brand based in Lisbon, Portugal, selling furniture, objects and lighting developed with designers such as Álvaro Siza Vieira, Manuel Aires Mateus and Christian Haas. The range includes the BULB and DOME lamps, and the pieces are made in Portugal.

The brand works with partner manufacturers in small-scale production lines, using small workshops, factories and traditional studios. Its materials include wood, leather, stone, glass and iron, drawing on Iberian woodworking and Czech hand-blown glass. The showroom is in Lisbon. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:minimalux.name: Minimalux
paragraphs: Minimalux is a British design brand making lighting, home objects and jewellery, including the Drum, NIL and ROTA lighting ranges. Its first collection was launched in Milan in 2009, and the brand was co-founded by the designer Mark Holmes, who trained at the Slade School of Art in London.

Production combines locally sourced industrial manufacturing with artisan techniques. The designs are built around function, form and calm order, and are meant to stay relevant beyond passing trends. The range also includes an Editions line. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:mass-productions.name: Mass Productions
paragraphs: Mass Productions is a furniture and accessories company in Stockholm, Sweden, founded in 2009 by Magnus Elebäck and Chris Martin. Its first product was the Tio chair, and the range now includes the Albert bar stool, the 4PM chaise and the Gridlock storage configurator.

Design is done in-house, and production runs through partner factories where the company works directly with engineers and machine operators, without an intermediary between designer and producer. Some products are offered for pre-order. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:cozmo.name: Cozmo
paragraphs: Cozmo is a British furniture brand with a showroom in Shoreditch, London. It sells modular sofas, armchairs, beds, tables and cushions, made in the UK. The range includes named sofa series such as Cozy, Float, Pillow and Rest, plus removable sofa jackets that change how a sofa looks.

Cozmo sells directly to customers online and offers up to nine free fabric swatches before an order. Customisation and easy assembly are central to the offer, and the sofas are designed to fit through standard doorways. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:graypants.name: Graypants
paragraphs: Graypants is a design studio and lighting maker with studios in Seattle and Amsterdam. It produces pendant, table, portable and linear lamps, along with architecture and other objects. The Scraplight series is handcrafted from recycled cardboard, mostly post-consumer waste, cut with lasers, assembled with non-toxic adhesive and treated with a fire retardant.

Alongside its main collections, Graypants designs custom lighting and large light installations for businesses. In the Netherlands it works with a social enterprise that provides craft-based jobs for people facing barriers to employment. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:giopato-coombes.name: Giopato & Coombes
paragraphs: Giopato & Coombes is a lighting design company based in Treviso, Italy. It makes lighting sculptures such as chandeliers, wall pieces and table lamps, grouped into named collections including Bolle Frosted, Soffio, Gem and Moonstone. Its stated aim is to bring the effect of light into living spaces.

Besides its collections, Giopato & Coombes offers unique pieces and custom-made work on commission for private and public spaces. Its commissions page lists projects from 2019 to 2023, including residences, restaurants and a hotel. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:tecta.name: Tecta
paragraphs: Tecta is a furniture maker in Lauenförde, Germany, run as a family business in its fourth generation. It makes cantilever chairs, wicker chairs, sofas, tables and lamps, and keeps a cantilever chair museum at its showroom. Metalwork, joinery, hand-weaving and upholstery are done in its own workshops, including its patented tube frames.

The workshops specialise in individual pieces, with adjusted dimensions, customer-supplied fabrics or leather and special functions. Tecta states that its furniture is made in Germany. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:noah.name: Noah
paragraphs: Noah is a furniture maker based in Berlin, Germany, founded in 2019. It makes modular sofas, beds, tables, a mirror and cushions, designed so that each part can be taken apart, replaced or extended without replacing the whole piece.

Pieces can be individualised from the start, and fabric and material samples can be ordered from the site. Noah is a member of the German Design Council (Rat für Formgebung). On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:wastberg.name: Wästberg
paragraphs: Wästberg, now trading as W+, is a lighting company based in Malmö, Sweden, and part of XAL Group. It makes ceiling, pendant, track, wall, table and floor luminaires, with named series such as Alma, Cast and Faro.

The collections are designed in collaboration with outside architects and designers, among them Inga Sempé, John Pawson, David Chipperfield and Claesson Koivisto Rune. The lighting is aimed at offices, hotels, homes and museum collections. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:se-collections.name: Sé Collections
paragraphs: Sé Collections is a London company founded in 2007 by Pavlo Schtakleff. It publishes contemporary furniture and lighting designed by invited designers, in four collections so far: by Damien Langlois-Meurinne, Jaime Hayon, Nika Zupanc and Ini Archibong.

The pieces are produced by a register of long-running European manufacturers, often family companies working with craft-based methods. The company also runs Gallery Sé in London, which shows collectible editions alongside work by artists and artisanal brands. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:pholc.name: Pholc
paragraphs: Pholc is a Swedish lighting brand founded in 2015 by Maja and Samuel Norburg. It makes pendant, floor, table, wall and ceiling lights, in collections including Apollo, Concave and Bounce.

The brand works with people from different fields on its designs. Its shop also sells spare parts and light sources for its luminaires. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:luke-malaney.name: Luke Malaney
paragraphs: Luke Malaney is a furniture maker who lives and works in Brooklyn, New York, and was born on Long Island. He trained under a classical Roman woodworker and applies traditional craft techniques in new ways, making work that sits between furniture and sculpture.

His pieces have been shown in solo, duo and group exhibitions since 2022, including a two-person show at Marc Straus Gallery in New York and, with Objective Gallery, at Design Miami and Thema Fair in Paris. Inquiries about commissions and collaborations go directly to him. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:buro-berger.name: Buro Berger
paragraphs: Buro Berger is a Dutch design label for home accessories, started by Gerbrand van Nijendaal and Berdien Righolt, who had earlier worked together at &Klevering. Since summer 2023 the label has been part of &Klevering, and its range includes the Dotty Mirrors.

The label works with designers and artists such as Bertjan Pot, Lex Pott, Carole Baijings and Nynke Tynagel, and collaborates with them from the first idea through to the finished product. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:la-chambre-d-ami.name: La Chambre d'Ami
paragraphs: La Chambre d'Ami is a French home decoration brand based in Rennes, Brittany. The designer, Rémi, creates and produces the objects in his own workshop, taking each one from first prototype to finished product. The range includes lamps in the Igloo, Pivoine, Méduse and Gaz series, as well as vases, soliflores and soap holders.

The brand redesigns everyday decorative objects into simplified, modular forms, and everything is made in France. Products are also sold through partner shops. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:kallemo.name: Källemo
paragraphs: Källemo is a Swedish furniture company based in Värnamo, founded in 1973 by Sven Lundh and run today by his daughter Karin Lundh. The collection covers chairs, armchairs and sofas, tables, shelves and cabinets, including the Ettore table by Åsa Jungnelius, which received the Born Classic prize.

Collections are aimed at architects and retailers who share a long-term view of quality, and the furniture is designed to outlast passing trends. The range includes a limited editions section and an archive of discontinued pieces. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:bocci.name: Bocci
paragraphs: Bocci is a lighting maker headquartered in Vancouver, Canada, founded in 2005 under the creative direction of Omer Arbel. It makes glass and metal lighting and installations, and numbers each project in the order it was conceived, so its lamps are grouped in series such as 14, 28 and 141.

Every object is developed, engineered and fabricated in-house at the Vancouver factory, and each piece is handmade and therefore unique. Bocci also offers an online configurator for building an installation to suit a space. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:art-resources.name: Art Resources
paragraphs: Art Resources is a family-owned maker of furniture, lighting, mirrors and decorative objects in Bangkok, Thailand, founded in 1989. Its pieces draw on Art Deco, combine simple geometric forms with local Thai craftsmanship, and use materials such as antiqued mirror, shagreen, rattan and bronze.

Bespoke work is a core service: a dedicated team guides clients through the available materials and builds custom pieces to the same standard as the standard range. The company has worked with interior designers and architects on residences and hotels. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:lemon-furniture.name: Lemon Furniture
paragraphs: Lemon is a furniture company based between Cape Town and Amsterdam, with showrooms in both cities open by appointment. It was founded by Kevin Frankental and Jaco van Staden and works with designers from around the world on tables, seating, bedroom pieces and lighting, in collections such as Tsu, Kent and La Plume.

Pieces are made with artisans including metalworkers, upholsterers and carpenters, and each one is made to order rather than mass-produced. Lemon also runs a trade program for interior designers. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:ceramicah.name: Ceramicah
paragraphs: Ceramicah is a lighting design studio in Los Angeles, run by partners Micah Blyckert and Alexandra Cadiz. It makes ceramic and wood lamps and sconces, including the Cuadra series of walnut or white oak fixtures with a perforated grid, and the Tera series of glazed and unglazed ceramic lamps.

Every piece is made by hand in the Los Angeles studio, and the studio sells directly as well as to trade customers, with a stockist list on its site. It has also made an outdoor Tera sconce in collaboration with ORCA. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:established-sons.name: Established & Sons
paragraphs: Established & Sons is a furniture and lighting brand with its address in Arnhem, the Netherlands. It produces chairs, daybeds, shelving, lamps, tables, rugs and objects in collaboration with designers such as Sebastian Wrong, Ronan & Erwan Bouroullec, Jasper Morrison and Konstantin Grcic.

Some pieces are released as limited editions, for example the Objects of Desire series. The collection runs from seating and storage to a vase and a clock. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:thorup-copenhagen.name: Thorup Copenhagen
paragraphs: Thorup Copenhagen is a Danish design brand based in Copenhagen and founded in 2018. It makes furniture and lighting, including the Mio tables, Noel chairs (also in a wool edition), Patrone lighting and Anto room dividers.

Production runs through a chain close to home, mostly in Denmark, combining traditional and newer techniques. The work is mainly made to order. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:petite-friture.name: Petite Friture
paragraphs: Petite Friture is a French design brand founded in 2009 by Amélie du Passage, with a showroom in Montreuil. It publishes furniture, lighting and decorative objects, among them the Vertigo pendant lamp, and has worked with more than 60 designers.

Pieces are produced with 37 manufacturers, 92 percent of them in Europe. The range is sold through a selective network of retailers in more than 70 countries. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:fleur-studios.name: Fleur Studios
paragraphs: Fleur Studios is an Australian furniture and homewares company with its head office on the Gold Coast and a warehouse in Greensboro, North Carolina. It designs coffee, side and dining tables, consoles and decor objects in marble and stainless steel, including the Oslo Collection.

Everything is designed in-house, and products are sold only through the company's own site, without retailers. Some items are offered for preorder. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:eilersen.name: Eilersen
paragraphs: Eilersen is a furniture maker based in Skamby, Denmark, with a history that goes back to 1895. It makes sofas, chairs, tables, shelves and accessories, and offers fabrics and leather for its upholstery. Its sofas are built on a solid pinewood frame, with timber oven-dried to a moisture content of 8-10 percent and traceable to FSC-certified sources.

The range is split into the main Eilersen collection and separate Contract, Outdoor and Viable lines. Eilersen has showrooms in Skamby and Copenhagen and a dealer section for trade customers. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:paola-paronetto.name: Paola Paronetto
paragraphs: Paola Paronetto is a ceramic artist with a workshop in Porcia, Italy, where she lives and works. She makes sculptural ceramic objects in paper clay, built up in layers and shaped to allow for imperfection. Her Cartocci collection dates from the early 2000s.

Her work has been shown in solo exhibitions at Ille Arts in New York and the Contemporary Ceramic Centre in London, and in a retrospective at the ADI Design Museum in Milan in 2021. Pieces are sold through showrooms, galleries and museum shops in Italy and abroad. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:omelette-editions.name: Omelette Editions
paragraphs: Omelette Editions is a furniture publisher founded in 2016 by the design studio La Mamba as a platform for its own designs. It offers sofas, poufs, armchairs, chairs, stools, tables and accessories, and about 98 percent of the collection is made in Spain.

The collection includes work by outside designers such as Francesc Rifé, Isern Serra and Isaac Piñeiro. Production and storage are located between Barcelona and Valencia, and some pieces are designed so their parts can be separated and recycled. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:arwenn.name: Arwenn
paragraphs: Arwenn is a furniture retailer in Berlin, Germany. It sells furniture, lighting and accessories, including chairs, lounge chairs, sofas, dining tables, desks, floor and table lamps, mirrors and vases. It runs a physical store in Berlin built around a gallery and warehouse concept.

Arwenn focuses on items that are available directly, so buyers can go from choosing to owning without a long wait. A separate business channel serves professionals, covering contract conditions, samples, customization and planning support. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:pulpo.name: Pulpo
paragraphs: Pulpo is a design company in Weil am Rhein, Germany, that publishes lighting, furniture, accessories and limited-edition art objects. Its pieces come from a group of international designers, among them Sebastian Herkner, whose Alwa table is part of the range.

Pieces are produced with partner manufacturers chosen for each material, and the range includes handmade ceramics such as the Chouchou Console, where variations in thickness and colour are expected. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:pode.name: Pode
paragraphs: Pode is a Dutch furniture brand and part of the Leolux Furniture Group. It offers sofas, modular sofas, armchairs, coffee tables, lighting and accessories by international designers, sharing a common visual language and colour palette. Recent additions include the Ono sofa and the Tinko armchair.

Leather, foam, wood and metal are bought from suppliers, every product carries a two-year guarantee, and the pieces are sold through dealers, with a Pode showroom at the Leolux Experience Center in Breukelen. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:ingridsdotter.name: Ingridsdotter
paragraphs: Ingridsdotter is a furniture and lamp brand in Stockholm, Sweden, founded in 2021 by Christine Ingridsdotter. The first collection is furniture by the designer Jonas Bohlin, and several pieces were made for Stockholm restaurants including Riche and Sturehof.

Pieces are produced in Sweden and offered in indoor and outdoor collections, through retailers such as NK and Nordiska Galleriet. The studio is at the Royal Swedish Academy of Fine Arts and is open by appointment. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:giacomo-tomazzi.name: Giacomo Tomazzi
paragraphs: Giácomo Tomazzi Studio is a design studio in São Paulo, Brazil, founded in 2017 by the designer Giácomo Tomazzi. It designs furniture, lighting and objects, including the Solar and Meraki collections and the Bo armchair.

Alongside an in-house line of authored pieces produced in limited series, the studio designs products for Brazilian brands including América Móveis, Breton and La Fonte. The Bo armchair also exists in a limited edition. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:oblure.name: Oblure
paragraphs: Oblure is a Swedish lighting brand based in Gothenburg, founded in 2017 by Markus Johansson and Erik Möller. It designs pendant, wall, table and floor lamps for homes and public spaces, and its first lamp, Cirrata, began as Johansson's thesis project in 2011.

Oblure develops its lamps together with international designers, among them Victor Castanera (Balance) and Färg & Blanch (Lightbone). Production is spread across several countries, with plans to grow manufacturing in Sweden. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:massimo-copenhagen.name: Massimo Copenhagen
paragraphs: Massimo Copenhagen is a Danish rug company based in Copenhagen with a showroom in Birkerød. It sells handmade contemporary rugs for private homes and public spaces, woven in India by weavers whose skills are passed down through generations, in materials such as bamboo, hemp, jute and wool.

The range runs to more than 350 variations, most of them held in stock, and the company also offers custom rugs for private and contract projects. Designer collaborations include Norm Architects and Space Copenhagen. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:kin-and-co.name: Kin and Co
paragraphs: Kin & Company is a design practice in Brooklyn, New York, run by cousins Joseph Vidich, an architect, and Kira de Paola, an interior designer. It makes sculptural metal furniture and objects, among them the Thin Series and the Crescent Table, and its first collection was shown in 2017.

The studio works with steel and tests the limits of the material, including research into oxidation and patinas, where chemical catalysts speed up the metal's natural oxidation to create surface patterns. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:arturel.name: Arturel
paragraphs: Arturel is a Danish acoustics and interiors company with its headquarters in Aabyhøj, Aarhus, and an office in Brooklyn, New York. It makes sound-absorbing wall art, acoustic tiles and rugs, including a series with upcycled wool textiles from Kvadrat framed in handmade solid oak.

The team researches, prototypes and produces its products, and works with collaborators such as Cody Hudson, Anne Nowak, Mandalaki and massimo copenhagen. Another series is made from upcycled uniforms of the Danish Royal Guards. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Acoustic wall art, tiles and rugs

makers:anour.name: Anour
paragraphs: Anour is a Danish lighting maker based in Copenhagen, producing handcrafted contemporary lamps in metals such as brass, copper, stainless steel and aluminium. The range covers ceiling, pendant, wall, table and floor lamps, and the I-MODEL, designed by founder Arash Nourinejad, is presented as its signature lamp.

Production takes place in Denmark, where craftspeople cut, shape, sand, oil and brush each piece by hand and assemble every lamp by hand; a single lamp takes several weeks to produce. The brand also supplies professionals and trade customers. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:kalmar-werkstatten.name: Kalmar Werkstätten
paragraphs: Kalmar Werkstätten is the product line of J.T. Kalmar, a family-run lighting maker founded in Vienna in 1881 by Julius August Kalmar and now in its fifth generation. Launched in 2009, the line makes pendant, table and floor luminaires based on designs from the company's archives, including the Posthorn pendant and the Kilo table lamp.

The archive pieces draw on the company's work with architects of the Austrian Werkbund and are updated for current interiors. The same company also runs Kalmar Project, which makes custom lighting for hospitality, commercial and marine clients. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:verk.name: Verk
paragraphs: Verk is a Swedish furniture brand with a showroom in Stockholm. It works only with Swedish raw materials, including Swedish wood, surface finishes, leather and wool, and all of its furniture is manufactured in Sweden.

The company was started by Simon Anund and Jacop Merlini and stresses traceability of materials and durability in its designs. It continues to look for new Swedish materials and collaborations. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:formarkivet.name: Formarkivet
paragraphs: Formarkivet is a Danish design house founded in 2023, with a showroom in Copenhagen. It designs furniture and lifestyle objects, from dining chairs, sofas and tables to lamps, rugs and tableware, and also sells a Marmacén home scent range that includes candles and reed diffusers.

Design is led by an in-house studio working with artisan partners across Europe. Formarkivet sells directly online and through retailers and contract dealers, with a digital showroom for professionals. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:deceres-studio.name: Deceres Studio
paragraphs: Deceres Studio is a design studio based in Mexico City and Southern California, founded in 2020 by Denise Martinez and Jorge Arturo Ibarra. It makes handcrafted objects for daily rituals, with monolithic forms, severe lines and narrow voids shaped by sacral and austere references.

Each piece is handcrafted, and the studio produces its work together with artisans in Mexico and California. It also runs a trade program for professionals and publishes a collection catalogue. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:astraeus-clarke.name: Astraeus Clarke
paragraphs: Astraeus Clarke is a design studio in Brooklyn, New York, founded by Chelsie and Jacob Starley, who moved there from Utah. It makes lighting, furniture and objects, and its lighting collections are built on simple geometry with unexpected functionality.

All pieces are handmade in Brooklyn by the studio's own manufacturing team. Each series is customizable, and customized pieces are handcrafted to order, with the process set up as a conversation between client and designer. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:cultivation-objects.name: Cultivation Objects
paragraphs: Cultivation Objects is the studio practice of Nathaniel Wojtalik in Brooklyn, New York, started in 2020. It makes objects that sit between art and functional design, including lighting such as the Nitka Lamp in aluminium and white oak, furniture, ceramics and door hardware in granite.

Wojtalik worked with sculptural, sound and video installations before the studio, and the studio uses atypical materials taken from the waste stream. His earlier work has been shown at IRCAM and the Berkeley Art Museum. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:motarasu.name: Motarasu
paragraphs: Motarasu is a Danish design house in Copenhagen, founded in 2019 by Mikkel Zebitz. It brings Danish and Japanese designers and craft traditions together in lighting, furniture and home objects, for example pendants with washi paper from the Mito region wrapped over fine resin strips.

The collection grows through collaborations with designers and makers such as Lars Vejen, Toshiyuki Tani and AHM x LUND, whose Ray lamp is in the permanent collection of Designmuseum Danmark. Bamboo shades are split, bent and placed by hand. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:lland.name: Lland
paragraphs: Lland (LA.LLand) is the architecture and object studio of Rachel Shillander in Los Angeles. It designs buildings, furniture, lighting, cabinet hardware and objects, including copper lamps formed from rolled, folded and stamped sheet metal and sculptural chairs cast in bronze.

Most lighting and furniture is made to order, with lead times from three to twenty weeks depending on the piece, and the bronze chairs are editioned. Custom orders are arranged through the studio. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:pulkra.name: Pulkra
paragraphs: Pulkra is a concrete design company in the Veneto region of Italy, with its office in Silea and its production site in Susegana. It makes furniture and objects such as the Multiplo Chair and the Dome Bathtub in ACRON, a composite concrete containing polymers and fine marble sand.

Pulkra works with designers and emerging artists, including Stormo Studio and Finemateria, and produces its pieces in limited editions. Under its Time Loop programme it takes back products at the end of their life so the material can be recycled. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:muhly.name: Muhly
paragraphs: Muhly is a design studio in Austin, Texas, founded in 2021 by two artists who moved into industrial and interior design. It designs wooden furniture, lighting and objects, using solid woods such as walnut, cherry and white oak alongside metals.

The collection is made by hand with partner makers in Philadelphia and Central Texas. Finish and size can be customised on most pieces, and the Austin showroom is open by appointment. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:monsieur-cailloux.name: Monsieur Cailloux
paragraphs: Monsieur Cailloux is a ceramic artist based in Paris, France, who began this work in 2020. The artist makes sculptural earthenware figures called Cailloux, presented as inhabitants of an imaginary planet named MRCX, each shown with its own number and measurements.

Every piece is hand-modelled and glazed, and is described as unique. The work has been shown in solo and group exhibitions, including at YTF Gallery in Taipei and Kaplan Projects in Mallorca. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:seer-studio.name: Seer Studio
paragraphs: Seer Studio is an interior design studio and furniture line in Austin, Texas, founded in 2020 by Scott Martin. Its furniture uses simple materials and form with little ornament, drawing on architectural shapes and European furniture designers from the 1930s to the 1970s.

Pieces are developed and built by hand with artisans and workshops in Central Texas. The studio also takes on custom projects for residential and commercial clients, including conference tables. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:palefire-studio.name: Palefire Studio
paragraphs: Palefire Studio is a lighting and homeware studio in London, led by founder and creative director Rowena Morgan-Cox. It makes table, wall, floor, pendant and chandelier lights, in collections such as Volta, U/V and one developed with 8 Holland Street. Its lamps are moulded from textured paper pulp and painted by hand in the London studio.

Each item is made to order, and design is handled in-house from concept through to shipping. The studio also advises on customisation and bespoke requests. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:joy-objects.name: Joy Objects
paragraphs: Joy Objects is a design company in Stockholm, Sweden, founded in 2021 around the designer Fredrik Paulsen. It makes furniture, objects and apparel, including chairs, benches, storage and side tables, and its Alu & Ghost collection is built around machined, anodized aluminium profiles.

Everything is designed and manufactured in Sweden. The furniture ships in flat packages with interchangeable parts, and the profile dimensions were optimised with Hydro Eco Design to use less material per object. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:superlife.name: Superlife
paragraphs: Superlife is a furniture and object brand in Yverdon-les-Bains, Switzerland, founded in 2014 by two designers from ECAL, with Edrris Gaaloul as creative director. It makes shelves, tables, lights, furniture and accessories, and began in a creative space made from his father's former forge.

Pieces are designed and made in Switzerland and produced in series. They are sold through the brand's online shop and through retailers. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:source-edition.name: Source Édition
paragraphs: Source Édition is a Paris house that reissues signed furniture, lighting and objects from the 1950s to the 1970s. It was founded by Isabelle de Ponfilly, formerly CEO of Vitra France, and Joséphine Bursacchi, who runs the Source Parisienne gallery for mid-century design. Its pieces include the Dialogue seating by André Monpoix and the TU-TU tables by Turenne Chevallereau, reissued with the Mobilier national, plus lamps by Ben Swildens.

Each reissue is made with the authorisation of the designer or their estate and comes with a certificate of authenticity. Production is in France and Italy. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:feldspar.name: Feldspar
paragraphs: Feldspar is a studio in rural Devon, England, run by Cath and Jeremy, who moved from London to Dartmoor in 2015 and began by making their own mug. It makes tableware, drinkware, vases and lighting in fine bone china, slip-cast and hand-painted in its own workshop, and has recently added a furniture collection by Jeremy in storm-felled local timber.

Feldspar also takes trade and bespoke commissions from interior designers, hotels and restaurants, and its work is sold through retailers including The Conran Shop, Selfridges, Fortnum & Mason and Harrods. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Bone china tableware, lighting and furniture

makers:faye-toogood.name: Faye Toogood
paragraphs: Faye Toogood MBE is a British artist and designer, born in 1977, who works in London. Her practice sits between functional object and sculpture, and draws on the shapes and materials of the English countryside. Her furniture and lighting includes the Gummy upholstered seating, the Roly Poly chairs and tables, the Spade stools and the Johnny lights.

Pieces are produced in the UK, with Gummy upholstered by hand in natural materials. The studio also considers bespoke dimensions, finishes and colours case by case, and she is represented by the gallery Friedman Benda. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:vibia.name: Vibia
paragraphs: Vibia is a lighting company born in Barcelona, founded there in 1987 by Joan Blanqué and Ernest Vidal. It sells in more than 105 countries, with subsidiaries in New Jersey and Singapore and commercial branches in London, Frankfurt and Dubai.

The range is organised by how a lamp is installed: pendants such as Asia, Bind and Circus, ceiling lamps such as Pro and Duo, and outdoor lamps such as Closer and Break. Vibia designs around thin construction, glue-free assembly so parts can be taken apart, low-voltage LEDs and interchangeable components. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Lighting: pendant, ceiling, wall, floor, table and outdoor lamps

makers:lee-broom.name: Lee Broom
paragraphs: Lee Broom is a London design brand founded by Lee Broom in 2007. He trained in fashion, worked for Vivienne Westwood and studied at Central Saint Martins before turning to furniture, lighting and accessories, and has since created more than 100 pieces.

The lighting range includes Hail, Vesper, Crescent, Fulcrum, Requiem and Orion, alongside furniture and accessories. Pieces are designed, manufactured and retailed under the Lee Broom name, with showrooms at Rivington Street in London and in New York. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:ross-gardam.name: Ross Gardam
paragraphs: Ross Gardam is a furniture and lighting studio in Brunswick, Melbourne, Australia, run by a team of designers, engineers and makers who work together from idea to finished piece. All products are designed and produced in Melbourne.

The lighting includes Aeris, Ceto, Liminal and Relic, and the furniture includes the Dwell, Hearth and Adapt lounge systems. Lights are hand-assembled in the studio from locally sourced glass, timber, ceramic and machined metal. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:wonderglass.name: WonderGlass
paragraphs: WonderGlass is a family business founded in 2013 in Italy by Maurizio and Christian Mussati, with a legal base in London and logistics in Resana, Italy. It works to keep the skills of Venetian master glassmakers alive, making glass by casting, fusing and blowing.

Lighting and objects come from collaborations with designers including Nao Tamura, John Pawson, Nendo, India Mahdavi, Marcel Wanders and Ronan and Erwan Bouroullec. It also takes bespoke and project work. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Collections, editions, art and bespoke projects

makers:frandsen.name: Frandsen
paragraphs: Frandsen is a Danish lighting company based in Horsens, Denmark. The collection is organised as pendant, table, ceiling, wall, floor, portable and outdoor lamps. Named series include the Ball pendants and wall lamps, the Lyss lamp series, Grasp, Flake, Nova and Hito.

Benny Frandsen is the company's founder, and the lamps are designed by a mix of designers, among them Toni Rie, Jonas Wagell, Friis & Moltke and Ida Tvede, together with Frandsen Design Studio. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:grupa.name: Grupa
paragraphs: Grupa is a design studio and manufacturer in Zagreb, Croatia, founded in 2006 by Filip Despot, Ivana Pavić and Tihana Taraba. In 2012 it began making its own lighting line, and its collections include Onda, Okolo, Arigato, Baluna and Ili Ili.

All Grupa products are designed by the studio and manufactured and assembled by hand in Croatia, mostly at a lighting factory that dates from 1960. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:sowden.name: SOWDEN
paragraphs: SOWDEN is the lighting and objects brand of George Sowden, who was born in Leeds, moved to Milan in 1970, opened his own studio there in 1979 and was a founding member of the Memphis Group in 1981. The brand dates from 2010 and is designed in Milan.

Its lamps are made of silicone and come in portable, table, ceiling and floor versions, the PL, TL, CL and FL series. The range also includes Pepper Salt and the Thing tables made with raawii. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:b-td.name: B-TD
paragraphs: B-TD, short for Ben-Tovim Design, is a lighting studio in Broadmeadows, Melbourne, begun by the industrial designer Jonathan Ben-Tovim with a few custom pieces for a friend's bar. It makes pendant, wall and portable lights, including the Reflector, Bloc and CARST collections and the Formation range.

Every piece is made to order, hand-assembled in the Melbourne studio and shipped worldwide, with finishes, sizes and technical details agreed through a quote. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Yes, finishes and details agreed per project

makers:gustaf-westman.name: Gustaf Westman
paragraphs: Gustaf Westman is a Stockholm design studio founded in 2020 by Gustaf Westman, who trained as an architect. It makes made-to-order furniture, ceramics and glassware in bold colours, from the Chunky tables, stools and tableware to the Curvy mirrors and sideboards, the Blob sofa and the Pipe chairs.

Furniture is made by hand by woodworkers in Sweden, ceramics in Portugal and glassware is hand-blown in the Czech Republic. Most pieces come in many colours, so here each model is shown once, in its calmest colourway, with the others listed. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:sons-design.name: Sons Design
paragraphs: Sons Design is a Swedish furniture maker in Dalsjöfors, started in 2019 by Robin Nilsson, who grew up in Borås. It designs and produces its own furniture, mainly in solid wood, and its MIND Collection includes the Sunflower Stool, the Temple Dining Table, the Wavy Coffee Table and the Bow Chair.

It uses FSC-marked timber, keeps its production line within 100 kilometres and plants trees for each order. It also takes custom projects, from dining tables and chairs to shelves and side tables. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

designers:salem-charabi.name: Salem Charabi
paragraphs: Salem Charabi (born 1992) is a Danish-Egyptian architect whose practice moves between Cairo and Copenhagen. With a small team of craftspeople he makes furniture and lights from materials found close at hand, among them Danish cherry, maple, beech, ash and Bavarian limestone, finished with linseed oil, earth pigments and ink.

Pieces are shown as small editions of 4 to 20, unique pieces and private commissions, and a studio exhibition in Copenhagen in June 2024 showed 38 pieces of furniture. Enquiries go to the studio by email. On Formground his work is shown through {count} works, each linked to his own website.
facts: Furniture and lighting, in small editions

makers:nanimarquina.name: nanimarquina
paragraphs: nanimarquina is a rug house founded in 1987 by Nani Marquina, which opened its first showroom in Barcelona in 2010. Its rugs are hand-knotted, hand-loomed or hand-tufted in India, Pakistan and Nepal, in wool, cotton, jute, nettle and recycled PET.

Designs come from Nani Marquina and from collaborators including Ronan and Erwan Bouroullec, Jaime Hayon, Eduardo Chillida and Lucia Eames. Chillida, Hayon x Nani, Lucia Eames, Mélange and Flora are among those shown here. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:kalon.name: Kalon
paragraphs: Kalon is a furniture studio founded in 2007 by Michaele Simmering and Johannes Pauwen and based in Los Angeles, with a showroom in Atwater Village that opened in 2021. It makes American-made furniture and objects in timber from sustainably managed forests, working with small regional teams of craftspeople.

Made-to-order pieces typically ship in six to twelve weeks. Rugosa, Material Studies, Highland and Caravan are among the collections shown here. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and objects in American hardwood

makers:fredericia.name: Fredericia
paragraphs: Fredericia is a Danish furniture company founded in 1911 in the city of Fredericia and still owned by the Graversen family. It began as Fredericia Stolefabrik, a chair factory, and from 1955 worked with Børge Mogensen, whose Spanish Chair and J39 are in the range. It acquired Erik Jørgensen in 2020.

Selected designs are produced in Fredericia and Svendborg, and the company is a certified B Corp. Spine, Delphi and Pato are among the pieces shown here. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:articolo.name: Articolo
paragraphs: Articolo is a lighting studio in Richmond, Melbourne, with a showroom in New York, led by founder and creative director Nicci Kavals. Kavals worked as a chef and food stylist and as Melbourne editor of Vogue Entertaining & Travel before moving into sculptural lighting.

All lighting is handcrafted in Australia and made to order, by artisans from Murano glassblowers to Australian metalworkers. Indi, Fini, Occhi and Saddle are among the pieces shown here. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:cvl.name: CVL
paragraphs: CVL Luminaires is a family-run company making brass lighting in its workshops near Angers, in the Pays de la Loire, since 1960. Collections are designed with Émilie Cathelineau, in-house designer, and with Sylvain Willenz, Pool Studio, Hervé Langlais and José Lévy.

Louis, Compass and Clopes are among the pieces shown here. José Lévy's Clopes 8 floor lamp was acquired for the Mobilier national in 2026. Custom-made work is also offered. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:david-pompa.name: David Pompa
paragraphs: David Pompa is a lighting studio in Mexico City, founded by the designer David Pompa Spikker, who studied product design at Kingston University in London. It makes pendant, table and wall lamps in black clay, volcanic stone, handwoven palm and hand-blown recycled glass, among them Can, Ambra, Origo, Amelia, Caleta and the Meta collection.

Components are made by craftspeople in different parts of Mexico, and the lamps are assembled and shipped from the workshop in the Roma Norte neighbourhood. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Lamps in clay, volcanic stone, palm and glass

makers:y-s-m.name: Y.S.M
paragraphs: Y.S.M PRODUCTS is the lighting brand of Y.S.M Co., Ltd., a lighting manufacturer in Yashio, Saitama, Japan, whose company dates from 1992. The brand was founded in 2017 and works with designers on lights built around metal: Moment by Kotaro Usugami, and-on by Kenji Fukushima, and NIGHT BOOK and LIGHT SHELF by Nao Iwamatsu and Takaaki Maeda.
The collection builds on the company's custom lighting work, and colours and engravings can be customised on request. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:mingardo.name: Mingardo
paragraphs: Mingardo is a metal furniture maker in Monselice, Padua, Italy. Daniele Mingardo launched the brand at Milan Design Week in 2013, from the blacksmith workshop his father Ilario opened in 1970. It makes small numbered editions in brass, copper, iron and steel, with designers including Simone Bonanni (Tartan), Elisa Honkanen (Shirudo), Chiara Andreatti (Satin Table), Marco Zito (Asse Zeta) and Omri Revesz (Fabbrica).
The workshop also builds custom-made furniture and metalwork for interiors, hotels and shops. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:benchmark-furniture.name: Benchmark Furniture
paragraphs: Benchmark Furniture is a furniture maker in Kintbury, Berkshire, England, founded by Sean Sutcliffe and Terence Conran, with workshops in Berkshire and Dorset. It makes tables, seating, storage, planters and beds, among them the OVO, Sage, Victoria, Gleda, Iklwa and Chico ranges, and takes bespoke commissions for commercial and residential projects.

Milling, cabinet making, veneering, upholstery and metalwork are done in the workshops, and an apprenticeship scheme has run for over 35 years. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

designers:jaime-hayon.name: Jaime Hayon
paragraphs: Jaime Hayon was born in Madrid in 1974 and trained in industrial design, with studies in Madrid and at the École Nationale Supérieure des Arts Décoratifs in Paris. Hayon Studio has its creative base in València, with offices in Barcelona and Treviso, and works across furniture, sculpture, installations and painting as well as interiors for hotels, restaurants and museums.

Pieces include the Monkey side table for BD Barcelona, the Talk talk rug for nanimarquina and the Catch lamp for &Tradition. On Formground Jaime Hayon is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Galerie Kreo, &Tradition, BD Barcelona and nanimarquina.
facts: Side tables, cabinets, rugs, lighting, ceramics (as shown on Formground)

designers:ronan-bouroullec.name: Ronan Bouroullec
paragraphs: Ronan Bouroullec was born in 1971 in Quimper, Brittany, and graduated from the École nationale supérieure des arts décoratifs in Paris. Since the late 1990s Ronan has worked with Erwan Bouroullec, a brother, in a studio in Paris. Their first industrial design projects came from Cappellini in 1997, and research work with Galerie kreo began in 2000.

Producers include Vitra, Artek, Alessi and Kvadrat. On Formground Ronan Bouroullec is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Galerie Kreo, BD Barcelona, Artek, nanimarquina and WonderGlass, among them tables, lamps, rugs and glass.
facts: Tables, lamps, mirrors, rugs, glass (as shown on Formground)

designers:erwan-bouroullec.name: Erwan Bouroullec
paragraphs: Erwan Bouroullec was born in 1976 in Quimper, Brittany, and studied at the École nationale supérieure d'arts de Cergy-Pontoise. After their studies Erwan began working with Ronan Bouroullec, a brother, in the late 1990s, and the two run a studio in Paris with a team of about six. Work with Vitra on the Joyn office system followed in 2002.

Together they have also designed for Kvadrat, Magis, Hay and Iittala. On Formground Erwan Bouroullec is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Galerie Kreo, Artek and Alessi, among them furniture and objects made with Ronan.
facts: Furniture and objects (as shown on Formground)

designers:jasper-morrison.name: Jasper Morrison
paragraphs: Jasper Morrison was born in London in 1959 and studied at Kingston Polytechnic, the Royal College of Art and the HdK in Berlin. In 1986 Morrison opened an Office for Design in London, which remains the base today, covering furniture, lighting, tableware, appliances and electronics.

Early manufacturers were Aram, SCP, Cappellini and FSB, followed by Vitra, Flos, Emeco, Magis, Maruni, Muji and Alessi. On Formground Jasper Morrison is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Alessi, Galerie Kreo and Fredericia, among them the Pots&Pans cookware, the Jota sofa and a three-legged stool.
facts: Cookware, sofas, stools, desks, tableware (as shown on Formground)

designers:stefano-giovannoni.name: Stefano Giovannoni
paragraphs: Stefano Giovannoni was born in La Spezia and graduated in architecture in Florence, where research and teaching at the faculty continued until 1991. Giovannoni Design is based in Milan and works across household products, furniture and more, with more than 300 steel and plastic products for Alessi, among them the Girotondo family.

The Bombo stool for Magis is another well-known design. On Formground Stefano Giovannoni is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Alessi and Ghidini 1961, among them the Mami cutlery and the Bold armchair.
facts: Kitchenware, armchairs, sofas, shelving (as shown on Formground)

designers:naoto-fukasawa.name: Naoto Fukasawa
paragraphs: Naoto Fukasawa was born in Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan, in 1956 and graduated from the Product Design Department of Tama Art University in 1980. Naoto Fukasawa Design was founded in 2003, and the practice has worked with more than 70 international and Japanese companies, among them Muji, Alessi, B&B Italia, Herman Miller, HAY, Vitra, Maruni and Plus Minus Zero.
On Formground Naoto Fukasawa is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Alessi and Galerie Kreo, among them the Itsumo and Cha tableware and the Chaos and Drilling tables.

designers:jonas-bohlin.name: Jonas Bohlin
paragraphs: Jonas Bohlin was born in Stockholm in 1953 and studied at Konstfack, the University College of Arts, Crafts and Design. The degree project in 1981 was the Concrete chair, made of steel and concrete, which became a reference point in debates about where art ends and craft or utility begins. Bohlin taught as a professor at Konstfack from 2004 to 2009 and received the Prins Eugen Medal in 2014.
On Formground Jonas Bohlin is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Ingridsdotter and Källemo, among them the Tivoli table, the Liv chair and the Concrete chair.
facts: Chairs, tables, lamps, stools, cabinets (as shown on Formground)

designers:alessandro-mendini.name: Alessandro Mendini
paragraphs: Alessandro Mendini (1931 to 2019) was an architect and designer born in Milan. Mendini graduated in architecture from the Politecnico di Milano in 1959, joined Studio Alchimia as a partner in 1978 and was editor-in-chief of Domus from 1979 to 1985. Casabella and Modo were also directed by Mendini.

From 1989 until 2019 Mendini ran Atelier Mendini in Milan with Francesco, a brother,. Architectural work included the Alessi factory in Omegna. On Formground Alessandro Mendini is credited on {count} pieces, shown through Alessi, Galerie Kreo and Baleri Italia, among them the Anna G. corkscrew and the Firenze table.
facts: Kitchenware, tables, stools, coat hangers (as shown on Formground)

designers:anderssen-voll.name: Anderssen & Voll
paragraphs: Anderssen & Voll is a design studio in Oslo, founded in 2009 by Torbjørn Anderssen and Espen Voll, who graduated from the Bergen Academy of Art and Design and the Oslo National Academy of the Arts. The studio designs furniture and objects for makers including Muuto, &Tradition, Røros Tweed, New Works and Vestre.
On Formground Anderssen & Voll are credited on {count} pieces, shown through &Tradition, among them the Pavilion, Ville, Massif and Meantime collections.
facts: Sofas, tables, chairs, trolleys (as shown on Formground)

designers:edward-barber-and-jay-osgerby.name: Edward Barber and Jay Osgerby
paragraphs: Edward Barber and Jay Osgerby studied architecture together at the Royal College of Art and founded their East London studio, Barber Osgerby, in 1996. Their work includes the Tip Ton and Mikado chairs for Vitra, the Plan Wood chair for Fredericia, the Bellhop lamp for Flos and the torch for the 2012 Olympic Games.
On Formground Edward Barber and Jay Osgerby are credited on {count} pieces, shown through Galerie Kreo and Fredericia, among them the Signal collection, the Hakone desk and the Plan tables.
facts: Chairs, tables, desks (as shown on Formground)

makers:resident.name: Resident
paragraphs: Resident is a furniture and lighting company based in Auckland, New Zealand, owned and run by its founders. It works with a group of designers including Asca Studio, Tim Rundle, Jamie McLellan, Philippe Malouin and NOTE, and the range includes the Sacha Sofa, the Radio Chair and the Cadre Chair.

Production runs through a network of workshops: lighting is made by a team in Auckland, timber furniture by joiners in Lithuania, and upholstery in London, Los Angeles and Melbourne. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and lighting by invited designers

makers:a-petersen.name: A. Petersen
paragraphs: A. Petersen is a Danish furniture company with its workshop, office and showroom in Korsør. Its furniture is designed, developed and produced in Denmark, in collaboration with designers including Chris L. Halstrøm, Line Depping, Knud Holscher, Ole Schjøll, Torben Skov and Dan Svarth.

Pieces shown here include the Tube Table, the Wire Table, the Metal Stool made with stylist and designer Anja Camilla Alajdi, and the Dining Chair in coloured ash. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:jaume-ramirez.name: Jaume Ramirez
paragraphs: Jaume Ramírez studio is based in Barcelona and designs furniture, lamps and accessories. It has worked with companies including Norman Copenhagen, Marset, Escofet and M114, and it quotes a line from Peter Brook about combining the closeness of reality with the distance of myth.

The objects shown here include the Sisa Bench, the Ele Armchair, the Kapla Chair, the Copérnica lamps, the Delica serving trays and the Ham Holder. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:heilig-objects.name: Heilig Objects
paragraphs: Heilig Objects is the studio of Daniel Heilig in Griesheim, Germany. He makes hand-signed single pieces, collections and limited editions of furniture and light objects, and design adaptations can be requested from him.

Materials include hand-oiled German maple, ash and oak, French walnut, Gampi vellum paper and illuminated fibreglass. Pieces shown include the PONTI Coffee Table, the THRONE Side Table, the FAT LEG 65 Dining Table and the PAGODE Naguri Stool. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:sekt.name: Sekt
paragraphs: Sekt is a maker of lighting and interior objects based in Malmö, Sweden. Its pieces are made by artisans in Sweden: mouth-blown in a glassworks, forged by a blacksmith, assembled by cabinetmakers or sand-cast in an art foundry.

The Glass Puritan pendants and table lamps come in colours such as Maroon, Tobacco, Old Rose, Ash and Dusty Green. Sekt calls its approach the craft of future antiques. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:mercoeur-editions.name: Mercoeur Editions
paragraphs: Mercoeur Editions is a French publisher of furniture and accessories in limited editions, working with designers including Grégoire de Lafforest, Mathieu Delacroix, Döppel Studio and Sébastien Kieffer. Pieces are made by craft workshops, many of them holders of the Entreprise du Patrimoine Vivant label, and finished and assembled in a workshop in the Paris region.

It follows in the footsteps of Biobject, which has worked with designers on collections for many years, and it also shows young talent. Pieces shown here include the Matera armchair and tables, the Arcy lamps, the Komorebi Steles and the Marigny Rug. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:calen-knauf.name: Calen Knauf
paragraphs: Calen Knauf is a Canadian designer living and working in Vancouver. He studied industrial design at Emily Carr University of Art and Design and has worked with companies including Tre Products, Tetra and Stussy.

The Trace Table and Wowtable are made by soaking vellum paper in epoxy resin, so each form is shaped by how the paper absorbs it, and the Fence Light is an adjustable table light with an oak base. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:jon-goulder.name: Jon Goulder
paragraphs: Jon Goulder is an Australian designer-maker who continues a four-generation legacy of furniture making. His practice covers one-off commissions, small-run furniture editions and complete interiors, working in leather, textiles and wood.

He was Senior Designer at Snøhetta from 2018 to 2024, and his work is held in museum collections including the National Gallery of Australia. Pieces shown here include the Pavilion chairs, the Broached chaise lounge and credenza, and the Avoca dining table and console. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:laun.name: Laun
paragraphs: LAUN is a Los Angeles design firm founded in 2018 by Rachel Bullock and Molly Purnell, who brought together backgrounds in woodworking, metalworking and architecture. LAUN Studio does architecture and interiors, and LAUN Objects makes furniture for indoor and outdoor use with Los Angeles manufacturers.

Pieces shown here include the Mondos club chair, chaise lounge and sofa, the Ribbon chair and stool, and the Butler table lamp. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture for indoor and outdoor use

makers:likemindedobjects.name: LikeMindedObjects
paragraphs: LikeMindedObjects, or LMO, is the design studio of artist Elise McMahon. It makes furniture, accessories and custom interiors using local materials and technologies, with a focus on healthier materials, less landfill waste and respectful labor practices.

McMahon trained in furniture design at Rhode Island School of Design and in industrial design at Parsons School of Design. Pieces shown here include the To-Go side tables, the Almost Nothing Floor Lamp, the CRCL Ottoman and a series of candlestick holders. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:orlando-pippig.name: Orlando Pippig
paragraphs: Orlando Pippig is a self-taught designer and fabricator based in Southern California, who opened his own studio in 2020 after nearly a decade of designing and fabricating furniture in wood and metal.

His designs follow a strict formal logic in which precise proportions, repetition and spacing produce minimal forms, and he studies connection methods closely. The work is numbered rather than named, from the TL-01 table lamp to the AL series of shelving, console and coffee tables. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and lighting in wood and metal

makers:mati-sipiora.name: Mati Sipiora
paragraphs: Mati Sipiora is a designer and craftsman who makes small-batch steel furniture and objects in his family's metalworking workshop in Czepino, Poland. He holds a PhD in design and worked in industrial design in Poznań and Berlin before returning to the workshop.

He works with a lathe, hydraulic press and welding equipment and avoids CNC machining. Pieces shown include the Poodle Armchair, the Cosmic Tray, the Zeppelin Chair and the Comet Lamp, and bespoke commissions are also taken. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:joe-armitage.name: Joe Armitage
paragraphs: Joe Armitage designs and manufactures lighting. The Armitage lamp collection was inspired by a floor lamp designed in 1952 by the architect Edward Armitage while he lived in Ludhiana, India, and is offered in a Classic and a Modernist range.

Joe Armitage and his team of designers and engineers also take on design and manufacturing for bespoke lighting features and hotel furniture schemes. Pieces shown include the Classic floor lamp, desk lamp and suspension lamps and the Modernist timber wall lamp. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:marbledworks.name: Marbledworks
paragraphs: Marbledworks is a Munich design studio founded in 2022 by Maximilian Huber and Dominic Kim. It makes furniture and accessories, much of it in natural stone, developed under in-house creative direction and including collaborations with selected designers and architects, all crafted in Germany.

The Sporadic Table is made from reclaimed stone offcuts and designed by AAS Gonzalez Haase. Other pieces include the Iso Table, the Jelly side table, the Hex Table System and the Brick and Bonkers objects. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:hyfer-objects.name: Hyfer Objects
paragraphs: Hyfer Objects is a design studio co-founded by Kristina Tjäder, Sara Stendebakken and Axel Andersson that turns waste materials into furniture and lighting. The main furniture material is about 70 percent wood scraps from Scandinavian and Baltic forestry combined with a recycled biopolymer.

The name comes from the Swedish word for hyphae, the fungal networks beneath a mushroom. Pieces shown include the Eel Lounge Chair, the Anemone and Octopus side tables, the Anemone dining table and the Kakta lamps, and bespoke pieces are also made. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and lighting from waste materials

makers:bleurenn.name: Bleurenn
paragraphs: Bleurenn, also written Bleu Renn, is a furniture studio in Sydney, Australia. Its work rests on three principles: considered design, quality materials and sustainable, ethical manufacturing, with craftsmanship carried out in Sydney.

The range includes the Acardia dining chair and ottomans, the Crescent dining tables in rectangular and round forms, and the Arbor, Koa and Calico Nest coffee tables. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:lukasz-korol.name: Łukasz Korol
paragraphs: Łukasz Korol is a furniture maker in Suwałki, Poland, who works in solid wood with hand tools and traditional joinery. Korol began in 2023 with the aim of showing unusual wood species in depth.

Each collection is a study of one species: Light of Sycamore, and In the Orchard, which covers pear, cherry and walnut. Pieces shown include the cabinet in ash, the desk in sycamore, the chest of drawers in cherry and the coffee table in walnut. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:studio-gameiro.name: Studio Gameiro
paragraphs: Studio Gameiro is an architecture, interior and furniture design studio in Lisbon, founded in 2018 by the architect João Gameiro. It works on the relationship between traditional artisanship, sustainable design and bespoke solutions, with projects across Western Europe.

Its collections include the MINE(ral) armchair and wall light, in patinated copper handmade in the Netherlands by Nick Valentijn, and the Alumina chair, stool and table. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:oven-editions.name: Oven Editions
paragraphs: Oven Editions is a small workshop in a mountain village near Valencia, Spain, making furniture and objects to order by hand from certified woods and other chosen materials. It was started by a founder who combines two interests, cooking and objects.

Pieces shown include the Sobremesa Round Table, the Serrin Rectangular Table, the Veta pendant and wall lamps, the Taula tray and the Moli salt and pepper mill. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Tables, lighting and kitchen objects in wood

makers:hokii.name: HOKII
paragraphs: HOKII is a Taiwanese home design brand whose name comes from the Taiwanese word for good fortune. It aims to make original designs available to many households, with designers drawing on everyday inconveniences, traditional crafts and traditional furniture, and it looks for new designers in Taiwan.

The two pieces shown here are the MOGU rechargeable portable wooden mushroom lamp and the 坐坐Q sleeping lamp, a collaboration with AH!Q. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:toh-studio.name: TOH-STUDIO
paragraphs: Toh is a Los Angeles studio experimenting in objects and furniture. The name translates as dirt, and the practice is a continuous study of objects through materials, balancing form and function on the belief that materials and processes give rise to form.

The piece shown here is the Ssang stool from the Study Aluminum series, made in 5052 aluminium in several sizes. Aluminium is chosen for its strength-to-weight ratio, its soft raw texture and because it can be recycled repeatedly. On Formground it is shown through one piece, linked to its own page.

makers:baleri-italia.name: Baleri Italia
paragraphs: Baleri Italia is a design furniture company founded on 8 March 1984 by Enrico Baleri and Marilisa Decimo, with its headquarters in Cantù, Italy. It built its name on work with designers including Philippe Starck, Hannes Wettstein, Angelo Mangiarotti and Alessandro Mendini.

The Cartoons screen received the Compasso d'Oro in 1994 and is in the permanent collection of the Museum of Modern Art in New York. The collection shown here includes the Juliette stools and chairs, the Spunta sofa and armchair, the Matteo modular unit and the Amiko coat hanger. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Chairs, sofas, tables and modular units

makers:alexis-ginger.name: Alexis & Ginger
paragraphs: Alexis & Ginger is a furniture and lighting design studio based in New York and founded by Ginger Gordon and Alexis Tingey. Their practice is built on research and material exploration, from carved wooden forms and textured textiles to inlay and stained glass.

The work is organised in collections including Amulet, Flora & Fauna, Sonnet, Silhouette and Ode, and ranges from the Waterlily and Iris mirrors to the Hand Cabinet and the Arp Stool. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:anna-dawson.name: Anna Dawson
paragraphs: Studio Anna Dawson designs lighting, with a few seating and home pieces, inspired by sensory experiences such as ocean air, morning light and urban discovery. The studio designs with emotion first and function second, and the work is found at places including Design Within Reach and the MoMA store.

The lamps are made of handmade fused glass, sometimes with hand-blown glass, on metal bases in stainless steel, brushed brass or blackened brass. Series include Ribbon, Twirl, Dancer, Calle and Valley, alongside the Portal bench and stool. On Formground their work is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:studio-sam-klemick.name: Studio Sam Klemick
paragraphs: Studio Sam Klemick is a Los Angeles furniture and object studio led by Sam Klemick, who spent 15 years in fashion before teaching herself to turn, carve and sculpt wood. A love of textiles runs through the work, from the lathe-turned Bell Chair to upholstered stools and pillows.

The studio works in two strands: the Series, made-to-order pieces such as the Bell Chair, and Singular, one-off hand-carved objects. Wood comes from salvaged Los Angeles construction sites and responsibly grown red oak, and every piece is handmade in Los Angeles. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.
facts: Furniture and objects in wood and textile

makers:fabrikant.name: Fabrikant
paragraphs: Fabrikant designs and makes furniture in Swedish stainless steel at its factory in Småland, with its address in Grimslöv. The factory has made stainless steel parts for commercial dishwashers for more than 30 years, and the Fabrikant brand carries that knowledge into furniture for public spaces, homes and gardens.

The steel is bent so that each piece ends where the next begins, with no waste, then welded and powder-coated for outdoor use. The range includes the BARR tables, benches and stools and the ROOTS line. All production is in Sweden. On Formground it is shown through {count} pieces, each linked to its own page.

makers:michael-felix.name: Michael Felix
paragraphs: Michael Felix is a furniture company that designs and produces upholstered pieces in Southern California, with a studio in Los Angeles. Michael is a third-generation upholstery designer who began as a sample-maker's assistant in the furniture factory his grandfather founded in 1959.
